name: HTTP Cache Inspector
description: Explain storage, freshness, age, Vary and validation offline; compare private and shared caches.
boundary: Offline simulation · ordinary GET/200 · same target URI · candidate assessment, not an observed cache hit

input.title: Configure experiment
input.name: Case name
input.timeHint: Example: 2026-10-22T10:00:00Z. Blank stays unknown; no device-clock substitution.
input.headerHint: One Name: value per line, without start lines or body. Up to 32 KiB / 128 lines per block.
input.sameRequest: Currently simulating the same headers as the original request. Enable the option above to compare a new request against Vary.
input.transient: Inputs stay in this page’s memory. No network access or response bodies.

result.title: Cache assessment
result.conditionalHint: ETag produces If-None-Match, Last-Modified produces If-Modified-Since. The former takes precedence. A 304 can refresh matching cached metadata for reuse; it is not a new body. Validation and metadata merging are not executed.
result.noValidators: No usable validators. Fetch a new response.
result.ageHint: Uses the conservative maximum for corrected initial age. Missing terms stay unknown; times use UTC seconds.
result.varyHint: Compare the original and new request in the selected case. * never matches; absent differs from present-empty. Sensitive values are masked.
result.noVary: No Vary fields are specified, adding no variant restriction.
result.maskHint: Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, proxy credentials and X-API-Key are masked. Malformed lines are excluded.
result.dirty: Inputs changed. Results below are from the last successful run; analyze again to compare.
result.empty: Why did this response miss expectations?
result.emptyHint: Enter headers and timing to compare storage, lifetime and validation constraints. All analysis runs locally.

messages.header_syntax: Line {{line}} of {{context}} headers is invalid. Start lines, bodies and folded lines are not accepted; assessment stays uncertain.
messages.singleton_duplicate: Singleton {{field}} occurs more than once. The last occurrence is not silently selected.
messages.control_syntax: Cache-Control in {{context}} contains incomplete quoting or syntax.
messages.delta_clamped: {{field}} exceeds the seconds range. It saturates at {{limit}} and cannot establish direct reuse.
messages.directive_invalid: Directive {{field}} in {{context}} has an invalid argument.
messages.directive_boundary: Directive {{field}} in {{context}} is outside this version’s scope, including extensions and field-qualified restrictions.
messages.directive_duplicate: Directive {{field}} occurs repeatedly in {{context}}; no silent last-value policy is applied.
messages.directives_limit: Cache directive count exceeds the limit.
messages.vary_invalid: Vary is invalid; the response variant cannot be confirmed.
messages.vary_conservative: Vary uses absence and conservative textual comparison. It does not infer arbitrary reordering, case or semantic equivalence.
messages.vary_match: Fields nominated by Vary match the stored request. Without Vary this adds no restriction.
messages.vary_different: Vary fields differ or include *. This candidate cannot be reused directly.
messages.time_missing: {{field}} is missing. Dependent terms remain unknown; the device clock is not substituted.
messages.date_missing: Date is absent. Apparent age and complete current age cannot be calculated without guessing origin time.
messages.date_invalid: Date is invalid or repeated and cannot establish a complete age calculation.
messages.age_first: For listed or repeated Age, the first member is used as specified; later members are discarded.
messages.age_invalid: Invalid Age is ignored as specified; the unavailable Age contribution is 0.
messages.age_absent: Age is absent and contributes 0. This does not prove that the origin was contacted.
messages.time_order: Time order must be request start ≤ response receipt ≤ simulated now. Age and remaining time stay unknown.
messages.date_future: Date is later than receipt. Apparent age is clamped to 0 as specified; clock skew is possible.
messages.freshness_invalid: {{field}} freshness is invalid or repeated. A conservative zero-lifetime policy is used, without fallback to lower-priority fields.
messages.expires_ignored: {{field}} takes precedence over Expires, which does not participate in this lifetime calculation.
messages.expires_received_date: When Expires exists without Date, lifetime uses Expires minus receipt time. Full age still retains its missing term.
messages.expires_invalid: Invalid Expires, including 0, or a repeated Expires is treated as expired with lifetime 0.
messages.no_heuristic: No explicit lifetime is present. A 200 response may still be stored, but this version does not estimate heuristic freshness.
messages.smaxage_private: A private cache ignores s-maxage and uses max-age, then Expires.
messages.public_private: public and private occur together. A shared cache follows the more restrictive private constraint.
messages.store_conflict: no-store coexists with cacheable markers. Storage prohibition wins except for the supported must-understand exception.
messages.scope_supported: This is an ordinary GET/200 without Range or Content-Range.
messages.scope_boundary: This version covers ordinary GET/200 only. Other methods, statuses and partial responses are outside scope.
messages.same_uri_complete: Assumes the same target URI and a complete 200 response. Bodies and actual cache keys are not inspected.
messages.must_understand_override: The 200 caching requirements are understood: response must-understand overrides response no-store. Request no-store still applies.
messages.no_store: no-store on the original request or response prohibits new storage, unlike no-cache which permits storage subject to validation.
messages.private_shared: Response private prohibits shared storage; private caches remain subject to other constraints.
messages.authorization_blocked: The original request has Authorization without explicit shared-cache permission via public, must-revalidate or valid s-maxage.
messages.authorization_allowed: The response explicitly permits shared handling of authenticated requests, subject to freshness, Vary and validation.
messages.storage_uncertain: Malformed input, field-qualified restrictions or scope prevent a definite storage assessment.
messages.storage_allowed: Storage is permitted by the covered rules. Permission does not guarantee storage or direct reuse.
messages.cookie_no_implicit_ban: Cookie/Set-Cookie do not automatically prohibit HTTP caching; directives, authorization and Vary still apply.
messages.pragma_boundary: Deprecated Pragma is present. HTTP/1.0 compatibility behavior is not simulated or equated to response Cache-Control.
messages.precondition_boundary: The new request already has preconditions. This version generates examples but does not evaluate client conditions or decide a 304 response.
messages.connection_boundary: Connection hop-by-hop fields are present. Their removal is not simulated, so reuse remains uncertain.
messages.same_request_assumed: No separate new request headers were supplied; an identical request is simulated.
messages.presented_no_store: New-request no-store prevents new storage but does not invalidate an already stored response; candidate reuse is still assessed.
messages.is_fresh: Lifetime is strictly greater than current age, so the response is fresh, subject to other reuse constraints.
messages.is_stale: Lifetime does not exceed current age, or is explicitly zero. The response is stale; serving stale is not simulated.
messages.freshness_unknown: Lifetime or required timing is unavailable; precise freshness and remaining time cannot be established.
messages.no_cache: Response or new-request no-cache calls for successful validation even while fresh. Request directives are honored as client preferences in this simulator.
messages.request_max_age: This simulator honors request max-age={{seconds}}: age must be ≤ {{seconds}} seconds and response freshness still applies.
messages.request_min_fresh: This simulator honors request min-fresh={{seconds}}: lifetime must be ≥ age + {{seconds}} seconds while the response remains fresh.
messages.stale_must_validate: The stale response is constrained by must-revalidate, shared proxy-revalidate or s-maxage and requires successful validation.
messages.presented_authorization: The presented request has Authorization without explicit shared permission, so direct reuse is not established.
messages.only_if_cached_unsatisfied: When honoring only-if-cached this candidate cannot directly satisfy the request; an appropriate failure, typically 504, is expected.
messages.no_validators: No valid validators are available. A full response or another real-cache policy is needed.
messages.validator_invalid: Invalid or unsupported-date {{field}} is excluded from conditional examples.
messages.legacy_date: {{field}} uses an obsolete two-digit year, requiring a reference-dependent century window. This version does not guess it; use a four-digit HTTP-date.

http-cache.headers_size: Each header block is limited to 32 KiB.
http-cache.fields_limit: Each block permits 128 nonempty header lines. Input was not truncated.
http-cache.scenario: Use a 1–80-character case name, a valid method token and a three-digit response status.
http-cache.time: {{field}} must be an offset timestamp from 1970–9999 with whole seconds, e.g. 2026-10-22T10:00:00Z.
http-cache.directives_limit: Each context permits at most 256 Cache-Control directives. Analysis stopped.
http-cache.expired: The analysis handle expired. Analyze again.
http-cache.export_limit: Report exceeds the 2 MiB export limit.
http-cache.copy_limit: Copy is limited to 64 KiB. Save a report file instead.

document.title: HTTP cache analysis report
document.boundary: Offline simulation · ordinary GET/200 · same target URI · candidate assessment, not an observed cache hit

help: Covers complete ordinary GET/200 for the same target URI. Storage permission, freshness and direct reuse differ. No requests or observed cache hits, heuristics, stale extensions, ranges, non-GET methods, 304 merging or vendor rules.

Configure a baseline, copy it to the experiment and change role, headers or timing. Compare analyzes both cases; disabling it analyzes the currently edited case. Input edits leave an explicitly marked old report until analysis runs again.

Headers use one Name: value line without start lines or body. An unset new-request block assumes identical headers; enabled-but-empty means an explicitly empty header set. Vary names are case-insensitive, while values use conservative comparison.

Timing requires explicit offsets and whole seconds. Missing terms stay unknown without device-clock substitution. Missing/invalid Age contributes 0; listed Age uses its first member. Lifetime precedence is shared s-maxage, max-age, then Expires. Invalid/repeated freshness is treated conservatively with diagnostics.

Request directives are honored as client preferences. no-store prohibits new storage; no-cache validates before use; must-revalidate constrains stale reuse. Authorization, qualified forms and unsupported directives are explained. If-None-Match takes precedence over If-Modified-Since.

Analyze 1–2 cases; each header context permits 32 KiB, 128 lines and 256 Cache-Control directives. Export is limited to 2 MiB and copy to 64 KiB. Inputs/reports remain transient without a new database. Exports always mask credentials, cookies, proxy credentials and API-key fields.

Date headers support four-digit IMF-fixdate and asctime, independent of local zones. Obsolete RFC 850 two-digit years require a reference-dependent century window and are explicitly outside this version’s scope.
